decision: Retain the independently named Hannon–Wally Section 4 guide; consolidate seven overlapping endpoint guides into exact selected access plans in the existing river hub.
rationale: Six adjacent endpoint pairs and two longer combinations shared one observation station and substantially repeated access/safety material. Different endpoints, lengths or summaries alone do not justify eight independent guides. Section 4 has a source-defined reach, length and seasonal outfitter restriction. Other choices remain useful for access research but are not independently verified itineraries.

sources.establishes: FWP names Hannon Memorial–Wally Crawford as Section 4, nine miles. Float outfitting is prohibited Mondays June 1–September 15. Public recreational users do not need the restricted-river commercial permit; separate access and fishing rules still apply.
sources.boundary: This does not ban all recreational floating, extend the outfitter restriction to the lower valley, or transfer the separate West Fork Section 1 Friday all-floating rule to Section 4.

sources.boundary: No visible publication date established; map states it is not suitable for navigation. It does not establish surveyed entry points or a present navigable channel.

distanceDecisions.decision: Retain numeric catalog estimates as explicitly unverified in labels, evidence and access-plan notes. Remove the false claim that FWP publishes every endpoint-pair distance.

Unresolved discrepancy is visible; neither 65 nor 72 is represented as a verified full-trip distance. Confirm stages before committing. Do not manufacture a replacement total.

preservation: All eight trip IDs, selected-access IDs, maps, geometry, original source URLs, hazard sets and coordinates remain available.
All eight remain planning-only with USGS 12350250 at Bell Crossing; no numeric recreational flow cutoff is introduced.
Original 2017 camping guide remains linked as historical context; current facility pages support the revised claims.
Seven old paths use existing instant meta-refresh delivery with hub canonicals and exact trip anchors; they are not HTTP 301 redirects.
Publication requires build, indexability, hydrated desktop/mobile selection, source-note preservation and both live serving paths. This source decision alone is not a release.
